Hi Ravi / Susan,

Hope you’re doing well — heading into your renewal window next month and I pulled a quick usage snapshot for Q2 attached (nebula_usage_q2.csv). Two observations: average GPU utilization across your dedicated pool is ~78% during peak hours, and your tail latency for 99th percentile increases sharply when sequence lengths spike (batching breaks down).

Given the growth you mentioned in the May roadmap, we should discuss either adding capacity or repartitioning slices to reduce contention on hot models. High-level options:
- Add a +12 A100-equivalent GPU tranche and enable staggered drain windows for safe rollout
- Repartition current fleet to isolate high-memory models and reclaim headroom for steady traffic
- Short-term burst credits to cover expected August spike while we finalize a sizing amendment

Can we schedule a 30-minute technical sizing call this week? I’ve cc’d Priyom (SE) and Ben (AE) so we can put a concrete addendum together.

Thanks,
Logan

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Renewal sizing and slice repartition for Nebula Health - Q3 addendum

Logan / Ravi — good thread. I dug into the usage file Logan shared and overlaid it with our per-model memory/latency profiles. Short technical summary and recommendation below.

Observations:
- Sustained peak utilization ~78% with frequent short bursts hitting >92% for ~3-6 minute windows.
- High-memory model (triage-v2) is causing KV-cache pressure and increases token-gen latency during concurrent requests.
- Current slotting mixes small/high-IO models with large/long-sequence models; this amplifies tail latency.

Recommendation (safe, minimal disruption):
1) Add 8 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs as an immediate tranche to cover forecasted August spike (this reduces average utilization to ~62% projected).
2) Repartition fleet into two slices: "high-memory" (triage + large-context) and "latency-optimized" (short chat/cli) — move 40% of current slots to high-memory slice.
3) Schedule a rolling drain over two maintenance windows (low-traffic UTC 03:00 - 06:00) to avoid client impact.
4) Create a short-term burst-credit line for September to handle any onboarding surges while the addendum completes.

I attached a compact implementation plan (inference_plan_v2.pdf) with estimated cost delta and expected latency improvement. If Nebula wants a more conservative approach, we can scope +12 GPUs instead of +8 — I left both numbers in the plan.

Ping me for the call — I can run a live profiling session with your logs if you share them.

Thanks,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ravi / Susan — thanks for the fast turn. Per Priyom’s recommendation I suggest we proceed with the conservative +8 tranche immediately and include an optional +4 tranchable within the addendum (i.e., client can trigger the additional +4 within 60 days with a simple invoice amendment). That keeps costs lower up-front while giving you runway.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll draft an addendum with the +8 baseline and optional +4 trigger and share for procurement review (Susan, I’ll include the cost delta and the short SLO note).
- Priyom will run the live profiling session on Monday to confirm expected tail improvements and finalize the drain plan.
- If you approve, Ben and I will route a DocuSign addendum for signature.

Susan — can you confirm the internal procurement timeline so we can align the DocuSign window?

Logan
